::: {.callout-important title="Instructor-only solution (not on the student site)"}
```python
def divergence(root, a, b):
    set_depths(root)
    root_age = max(l.depth for l in root.leaves())
    return root_age - clade(root, [a, b]).depth

split = divergence(euk, "Mammalia", "Aves")
print(f"Mammalia-Aves split in the eukaryote class tree: {split:.1f} Mya")
print(f"Amniote root in the family-level file:           319.0 Mya")
```

Expected: both lines read 319.0 Mya. The mammal–bird split *is* the
amniote root — mammals sit on one side of the first amniote fork, birds
on the other, so the two questions are the same question. The files
agree to the decimal because both are views of TimeTree's single
consensus: consistency, not independent confirmation. Independence would
require dates derived from different data and methods (different
calibrating fossils, different genes/studies). Common error: returning
`clade(...).depth` directly (depth-since-root instead of age-before-
present).
